_note: Layered India map modules. Layer kinds: states (state/UT names), pins (lat/lon, approximate, for teaching), features (Natural Earth 10m region names), lines (schematic routes through lat/lon points). 'groups' colours states in two shades.

modules.name: Physical India
modules.seo: Physical map of India for UPSC Mains
modules.desc: Physical India map for UPSC Mains: Himalayan and peninsular ranges, plateaus, plains, desert, coasts and deltas, mountain passes and peaks, with a locate quiz and PYQ sketch drills.
modules.lead: Every geography answer rests on this frame: the young Himalayas in the north, the old peninsular block in the south, the alluvial plains between them, and the coasts and islands around. Switch layers, tap a feature, then test yourself.

layers.name: Mountains & hills
layers.note: The Himalaya–Karakoram arc is young fold mountains; the Aravallis are among the oldest ranges on Earth; the Vindhyas and Satpuras divide north from south India; the Western Ghats are a steep escarpment, the Eastern Ghats a broken line of hills.

layers.name: Plateaus, plains & desert
layers.note: The Deccan and Chota Nagpur plateaus hold most of India's minerals; the Indo-Gangetic plain is the agricultural core; the Thar is India's hot desert.

layers.name: Coasts & deltas
layers.note: The west coast is narrow and cut by estuaries; the east coast is broad, with the big deltas of the Ganga–Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.

layers.name: Passes
layers.note: Himalayan passes carry trade, pilgrimage and military routes; the Palghat Gap is the main break in the Western Ghats.

items.name: Karakoram Pass
items.note: Ladakh–Xinjiang; historic Silk Road branch.

items.name: Khardung La
items.note: Ladakh; road to the Nubra valley and Siachen.

items.name: Zoji La
items.note: Links the Kashmir valley with Ladakh; a tunnel is being built beneath it.

items.name: Banihal
items.note: Pir Panjal crossing between Jammu and the Kashmir valley.

items.name: Rohtang
items.note: Himachal Pradesh, Kullu to Lahaul; bypassed by the Atal Tunnel.

items.name: Shipki La
items.note: Himachal Pradesh–Tibet trade pass, along the Sutlej.

items.name: Lipulekh
items.note: Uttarakhand–Tibet; Kailash Mansarovar route; Nepal disputes the area.

items.name: Nathu La
items.note: Sikkim–Tibet; trade route and Kailash yatra route.

items.name: Bomdi La
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh, on the road to Tawang.

items.name: Palghat Gap
items.note: Break in the Western Ghats linking Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

items.name: Bhor Ghat
items.note: Western Ghats pass on the Mumbai–Pune route.

layers.name: Peaks
layers.note: Highest points of each block: K2 in the Karakoram, Kangchenjunga in the Himalaya, Anamudi in the south.

items.name: K2 (Godwin-Austen)
items.note: Highest peak in India's territory (Karakoram, in Gilgit-Baltistan).

items.name: Kangchenjunga
items.note: Highest peak of the Indian Himalaya, on the Sikkim–Nepal border.

items.name: Nanda Devi
items.note: Uttarakhand; core of a biosphere reserve.

items.name: Anamudi
items.note: Highest peak in peninsular India, Kerala.

items.name: Doddabetta
items.note: Highest point of the Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu.

items.name: Guru Shikhar
items.note: Highest point of the Aravallis, Mount Abu, Rajasthan.

layers.name: Islands
layers.note: Andaman & Nicobar are the peaks of a submerged range; Lakshadweep is coral atolls.

modules.name: Climate, monsoon & soils
modules.seo: Monsoon, climate & soil map of India for UPSC
modules.desc: Monsoon, climate and soil map of India for UPSC Mains: the two monsoon branches, rainfall extremes, the north-east monsoon, and the main soil regions, with PYQ sketch drills.
modules.lead: The monsoon arrives in two branches, gets blocked or squeezed by relief, and leaves a map of wet and dry places that decides soils, crops and hazards. These maps are schematic, as you would draw them in an answer.

layers.name: Monsoon branches
layers.note: Schematic. The Arabian Sea branch hits the Western Ghats and moves inland; the Bay of Bengal branch is funnelled into the North-East and turned west along the Himalaya, which is why Bihar's monsoon blows from the east (Purvaiya).

items.name: Arabian Sea branch
items.note: Brings heavy rain to the windward Western Ghats; the Deccan interior lies in rain shadow.

items.name: Bay of Bengal branch
items.note: Turns west along the Himalaya; rain decreases from east to west across the Ganga plain.

layers.name: Rainfall extremes
layers.note: Relief explains the extremes: the funnel-shaped Khasi hills catch the Bay branch, while Ladakh and western Rajasthan lie beyond the reach of moist winds.

items.name: Mawsynram
items.note: Among the wettest places on Earth, on the southern Khasi hills.

items.name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
items.note: Next to Mawsynram; record rainfall from orographic lifting.

items.name: Agumbe
items.note: Very wet windward slope of the Western Ghats, Karnataka.

items.name: Jaisalmer
items.note: Hot desert: the Arabian Sea branch runs parallel to the Aravallis and drops little rain.

items.name: Leh
items.note: Cold desert in the rain shadow of the Himalaya.

layers.name: North-east (winter) monsoon
layers.note: Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain from October to December, when retreating north-east winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

layers.name: Alluvial soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. Deposited by Himalayan rivers; India's most widespread and fertile soil.

layers.name: Black (regur) soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. Weathered Deccan basalt; holds moisture and suits cotton.

layers.name: Red & yellow soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. On old crystalline rocks of the eastern and southern peninsula; low in nitrogen.

layers.name: Laterite soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. Leached in hot, very wet areas; used for cashew, tea and coffee.

layers.name: Desert soils
layers.note: Sandy, saline and low in organic matter.

modules.name: Hazard zones
modules.seo: Disaster hazard zone map of India for UPSC
modules.desc: Hazard map of India for UPSC Mains: seismic zone V, cyclone-prone coasts, flood-, drought- and landslide-prone states, and major disasters since 1984, with PYQ sketch drills.
modules.lead: Disaster management answers score with a quick vulnerability sketch. These layers show where each hazard concentrates, at state level, and where the major disasters of recent decades struck.

layers.name: Seismic zone V
layers.note: Highest-risk zone in the long-standing BIS zoning (IS 1893). Shown by state: dark = whole state, light = parts. BIS has been revising the zoning, so check the current map before quoting it.

layers.name: Cyclone-prone coasts
layers.note: The east coast faces more and stronger cyclones; Arabian Sea cyclones are fewer but growing stronger as the sea warms.

layers.name: Flood-prone
layers.note: The Brahmaputra and Ganga plains flood almost every year; urban floods now add to this map.

layers.name: Drought-prone
layers.note: Approximate, by state. Large rain-shadow and arid areas: western Rajasthan, Kutch, Marathwada, north Karnataka, Rayalaseema, Telangana.

layers.name: Landslide-prone
layers.note: Two belts: the young, seismic Himalaya and the steep, rain-soaked Western Ghats.

layers.name: Major disasters
layers.note: Case studies UPSC answers often cite.

items.name: Bhopal gas leak (1984)
items.note: Industrial disaster; led to new environmental and liability laws.

items.name: Latur earthquake (1993)
items.note: Struck the 'stable' Deccan plateau, in what was then rated a low-risk zone.

items.name: Odisha super cyclone (1999)
items.note: About 10,000 deaths; Odisha's later preparedness became a model.

items.name: Bhuj earthquake (2001)
items.note: Together with the 2004 tsunami, pushed India towards the Disaster Management Act, 2005.

items.name: Indian Ocean tsunami (2004)
items.note: Hit the Tamil Nadu coast (Nagapattinam) and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

items.name: Mumbai floods (2005)
items.note: Extreme rain on a city that had built over drains and the Mithi river.

items.name: Kedarnath (2013)
items.note: Cloudburst and glacial lake burst in Uttarakhand.

items.name: Chennai floods (2015)
items.note: Encroached lakes and wetlands turned heavy rain into a flood.

items.name: Kerala floods (2018)
items.note: Heaviest floods in Kerala in about a century; landslides across the Ghats.

items.name: Joshimath subsidence (2023)
items.note: Town sinking on old landslide debris; questions over Himalayan construction.

items.name: Wayanad landslides (2024)
items.note: Deadly landslides after extreme rain in the Western Ghats.

modules.name: Resources & agriculture
modules.seo: Minerals, energy & crops map of India for UPSC
modules.desc: Resources map of India for UPSC Mains: coal, iron ore and bauxite belts, oil and gas fields, and major crop states for rice, wheat, sugarcane, cotton, tea, coffee and jute.
modules.lead: Resource distribution is a GS1 syllabus line, and agriculture questions in GS3 keep asking why crops grow where they do. Minerals cluster in the old peninsular rocks; crops follow soils, water and markets.

layers.name: Coal
layers.note: Almost all of India's coal lies in Gondwana rocks along the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari valleys; Neyveli has lignite.

items.name: Jharia
items.note: Jharkhand; India's main coking-coal field, with long-burning underground fires.

items.name: Raniganj
items.note: West Bengal; India's oldest coalfield (Damodar valley).

items.name: Korba
items.note: Chhattisgarh; pithead power plants.

items.name: Talcher
items.note: Odisha (Mahanadi valley).

items.name: Singrauli
items.note: Madhya Pradesh–Uttar Pradesh; India's 'energy capital'.

items.name: Singareni
items.note: Telangana (Godavari valley).

items.name: Neyveli
items.note: Tamil Nadu; lignite (brown coal).

layers.name: Iron ore
layers.note: High-grade haematite in the old Dharwar rocks of Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Goa.

items.name: Keonjhar
items.note: Odisha; part of India's richest iron ore belt.

items.name: Noamundi
items.note: Jharkhand (Singhbhum).

items.name: Bailadila
items.note: Chhattisgarh; high-grade ore in the Bastar hills.

items.name: Ballari–Hospet
items.note: Karnataka; scene of the illegal mining case.

items.name: Goa mines
items.note: Export-oriented ore; mining paused by court orders.

layers.name: Bauxite
layers.note: Aluminium ore on the flat-topped Eastern Ghats and plateaus; mining often clashes with tribal rights.

items.name: Panchpatmali (Koraput)
items.note: Odisha; one of India's largest bauxite deposits.

items.name: Niyamgiri
items.note: Odisha; Dongria Kondh gram sabhas rejected mining in 2013.

items.name: Lohardaga
items.note: Jharkhand (Chota Nagpur).

layers.name: Oil & gas fields
layers.note: India produces a small share of the oil it uses, from sedimentary basins on land and offshore.

items.name: Mumbai High
items.note: Offshore field; India's largest oil producer.

items.name: Digboi
items.note: Assam; oil found in the 1880s, refinery since 1901.

items.name: Ankleshwar
items.note: Gujarat (Cambay basin).

items.name: Barmer (Mangala)
items.note: Rajasthan; largest onshore find of recent decades.

items.name: Krishna–Godavari basin
items.note: Offshore gas off Andhra Pradesh.

layers.name: Rice states
layers.note: Major producers; the order changes year to year.

layers.name: Wheat states
layers.note: Major producers; a rabi crop of the north-west and central plains.

layers.name: Sugarcane states
layers.note: Uttar Pradesh leads on area; the south (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) gets higher yields and a longer crushing season.

layers.name: Cotton states
layers.note: Mostly on black soils of the Deccan and in the irrigated north-west.

layers.name: Tea & coffee
layers.note: Tea in Assam, the Darjeeling hills and the Nilgiris; coffee in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

layers.name: Jute states
layers.note: Warm, humid Ganga–Brahmaputra delta lands.

modules.name: Industry & infrastructure
modules.seo: Industrial corridors, ports & steel plants map of India
modules.desc: Industry and infrastructure map of India for UPSC Mains: integrated steel plants, oil refineries, the 12 major ports, dedicated freight corridors and industrial corridors.
modules.lead: Industrial location questions ask why plants sit where they do: near raw materials, ports or markets. Infrastructure questions ask how corridors and ports tie them together.

layers.name: Steel plants
layers.note: Older plants sit on the eastern coal–iron belt; newer ones prefer ports (Visakhapatnam, Kalinganagar) or ore fields (Vijayanagar).

items.name: Jamshedpur (Tata Steel)
items.note: Founded in 1907; India's first large steel plant, near iron ore and coal.

items.name: Bhilai
items.note: Chhattisgarh; built with Soviet help (1959).

items.name: Rourkela
items.note: Odisha; built with German help.

items.name: Durgapur
items.note: West Bengal; built with British help.

items.name: Bokaro
items.note: Jharkhand; built with Soviet help.

items.name: Visakhapatnam (RINL)
items.note: First shore-based integrated steel plant.

items.name: Kalinganagar
items.note: Odisha; new steel hub near Paradip port.

items.name: Vijayanagar (JSW)
items.note: Karnataka; next to the Ballari ore fields.

layers.name: Refineries
layers.note: Most refineries sit at ports or near big markets, not near oil fields, because India imports most of its crude.

items.name: Jamnagar
items.note: Gujarat; the world's largest refining complex, at the coast.

items.name: Digboi
items.note: Assam; India's oldest refinery (1901).

items.name: Panipat
items.note: Haryana; market-based, fed by pipeline.

items.name: Mathura
items.note: Uttar Pradesh; emissions threat to the Taj debated in court.

items.name: Barauni
items.note: Bihar.

items.name: Haldia
items.note: West Bengal; port-based.

items.name: Paradip
items.note: Odisha; port-based.

items.name: Kochi
items.note: Kerala; port-based.

items.name: Mangaluru
items.note: Karnataka; port-based.

items.name: Numaligarh
items.note: Assam; set up under the Assam Accord.

layers.name: Major ports
layers.note: The 12 major ports under the Union government. Vadhavan, under construction in Maharashtra, will add a new deep-draft port.

items.name: Deendayal (Kandla)
items.note: Gujarat; tidal port built after Partition to replace Karachi.

items.name: Mumbai
items.note: Natural harbour.

items.name: JNPA (Nhava Sheva)
items.note: India's leading container port.

items.name: Mormugao
items.note: Goa; iron ore exports.

items.name: New Mangalore
items.note: Karnataka.

items.name: Cochin
items.note: Kerala; Vallarpadam transhipment terminal.

items.name: V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin)
items.note: Tamil Nadu.

items.name: Chennai
items.note: Artificial harbour.

items.name: Kamarajar (Ennore)
items.note: Tamil Nadu; first corporatised major port.

items.name: Visakhapatnam
items.note: Deepest land-locked harbour on the east coast.

items.name: Paradip
items.note: Odisha; coal and iron ore.

items.name: Kolkata–Haldia
items.note: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port; India's only major river port.

layers.name: Dedicated freight corridors
layers.note: Schematic. Freight-only railways that free the main lines for passenger trains.

items.name: Eastern DFC
items.note: Ludhiana to Sonnagar (Bihar); carries coal and grain.

items.name: Western DFC
items.note: Dadri (near Delhi) to JNPA, Mumbai; double-stack container trains.

layers.name: Industrial corridors
layers.note: Schematic. Planned manufacturing belts with industrial cities along major freight routes.

items.name: Delhi–Mumbai (DMIC)
items.note: Built along the Western DFC; Dholera and Shendra–Bidkin are new cities on it.

items.name: Amritsar–Kolkata (AKIC)
items.note: Built along the Eastern DFC.

items.name: Chennai–Bengaluru (CBIC)
items.note: Links two of India's biggest manufacturing cities.

items.name: Bengaluru–Mumbai (BMEC)
items.note: Economic corridor across western Karnataka and Maharashtra.

items.name: Vizag–Chennai (VCIC)
items.note: First phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor.

modules.name: History on the map: India
modules.seo: Indian history & culture places map for UPSC Mains
modules.desc: Indian history and culture map for UPSC Mains: Harappan sites, Buddhist sites, temples and monuments, centres of the 1857 revolt, Gandhian movements and tribal–peasant revolts.
modules.lead: Art & culture and modern history answers gain marks when a place is pinned correctly: a Harappan site in Gujarat, a Chola temple on the Kaveri, the Champaran satyagraha in Bihar. Pins are approximate.

layers.name: Harappan sites
layers.note: Most Harappan sites lie along the Indus and the Ghaggar–Hakra; Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are now in Pakistan.

items.name: Harappa
items.note: Punjab, Pakistan; first site excavated (1921), on the Ravi.

items.name: Mohenjo-daro
items.note: Sindh, Pakistan; Great Bath, planned grid.

items.name: Dholavira
items.note: Kutch, Gujarat; water reservoirs; World Heritage Site (2021).

items.name: Lothal
items.note: Gujarat; dockyard; a national maritime heritage complex is being built.

items.name: Kalibangan
items.note: Rajasthan; ploughed field and fire altars.

items.name: Rakhigarhi
items.note: Haryana; among the largest Harappan sites.

items.name: Banawali
items.note: Haryana; clay plough model.

items.name: Ropar
items.note: Punjab, on the Sutlej.

layers.name: Buddhist sites
layers.note: The Buddha's life sites cluster in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh; stupas and caves spread his teaching across India.

items.name: Lumbini
items.note: Nepal; the Buddha's birthplace.

items.name: Bodh Gaya
items.note: Bihar; enlightenment; Mahabodhi temple.

items.name: Sarnath
items.note: Uttar Pradesh; first sermon; Ashokan lion capital.

items.name: Kushinagar
items.note: Uttar Pradesh; mahaparinirvana.

items.name: Nalanda
items.note: Bihar; ancient university; revived in 2014.

items.name: Sanchi
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; Great Stupa with carved gateways.

items.name: Ajanta
items.note: Maharashtra; Buddhist caves with murals.

layers.name: Temples & monuments
layers.note: Nagara temples in the north, Dravida in the south, Vesara in the Deccan.

items.name: Khajuraho
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; Chandela temples, Nagara style.

items.name: Konark
items.note: Odisha; Sun temple shaped as a chariot.

items.name: Mamallapuram
items.note: Tamil Nadu; Pallava rathas and Shore Temple.

items.name: Kanchipuram
items.note: Tamil Nadu; Pallava capital, Kailasanatha temple.

items.name: Thanjavur
items.note: Tamil Nadu; Chola Brihadeeswara temple.

items.name: Hampi
items.note: Karnataka; Vijayanagara capital.

items.name: Pattadakal
items.note: Karnataka; Chalukya temples mixing Nagara and Dravida.

items.name: Ellora
items.note: Maharashtra; rock-cut Kailasa temple; Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.

items.name: Fatehpur Sikri
items.note: Uttar Pradesh; Akbar's capital.

layers.name: Revolt of 1857
layers.note: The revolt spread from Meerut across the Ganga plain and central India.

items.name: Barrackpore
items.note: Mangal Pandey's revolt, March 1857.

items.name: Meerut
items.note: Sepoys rose on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi.

items.name: Delhi
items.note: Bahadur Shah Zafar proclaimed emperor.

items.name: Kanpur
items.note: Nana Saheb and Tantia Tope.

items.name: Lucknow
items.note: Begum Hazrat Mahal.

items.name: Jhansi
items.note: Rani Lakshmibai.

items.name: Arrah
items.note: Kunwar Singh, Bihar.

items.name: Bareilly
items.note: Khan Bahadur Khan.

layers.name: Gandhian movements
layers.note: From local satyagrahas (1917–18) to mass movements (1920–42).

items.name: Champaran
items.note: Bihar, 1917; indigo farmers; Gandhi's first satyagraha in India.

items.name: Kheda
items.note: Gujarat, 1918; revenue relief after crop failure.

items.name: Ahmedabad
items.note: Gujarat, 1918; mill workers' strike.

items.name: Amritsar (Jallianwala Bagh)
items.note: Punjab, 1919; massacre after the Rowlatt protests.

items.name: Chauri Chaura
items.note: Uttar Pradesh, 1922; violence led Gandhi to call off Non-Cooperation.

items.name: Bardoli
items.note: Gujarat, 1928; Patel's no-tax campaign.

items.name: Dandi
items.note: Gujarat, 1930; the Salt March begins Civil Disobedience.

items.name: Bombay (Gowalia Tank)
items.note: 1942; Quit India resolution.

layers.name: Tribal & peasant revolts
layers.note: Resistance to colonial land, forest and revenue policies.

items.name: Santhal hul (1855–56)
items.note: Rajmahal hills, Jharkhand; Sidhu and Kanhu.

items.name: Munda ulgulan (1899–1900)
items.note: Around Ranchi and Khunti; Birsa Munda.

items.note: Andhra hills; Alluri Sitarama Raju.

items.name: Indigo revolt (1859–60)
items.note: Nadia, Bengal; against forced indigo cultivation.

items.name: Moplah rebellion (1921)
items.note: Malabar, Kerala; peasants against landlords and the state.

modules.name: Society & polity on the map
modules.seo: Fifth & Sixth Schedule, Article 371 and new states map
modules.desc: Polity and society map of India for UPSC Mains: Fifth and Sixth Schedule states, Article 371 special provisions, states formed after 1956, Union Territories and sex-ratio extremes.
modules.lead: Federalism, tribal and social justice questions often turn on where a provision applies. These layers map the Schedules, the Article 371 states, India's newer states and its Union Territories.

layers.name: Sixth Schedule
layers.note: Autonomous district councils in tribal areas of four North-Eastern states (Article 244(2)). Ladakh's demand for it is a live issue.

layers.name: Fifth Schedule
layers.note: Scheduled Areas in ten states (Article 244(1)), with Tribes Advisory Councils and the PESA Act, 1996.

layers.name: Article 371 states
layers.note: Special provisions for particular states, from development boards (371) to protection of customary law (371A Nagaland, 371G Mizoram). Tap a state for its clause.

stateNotes.Maharashtra: Article 371(2): development boards for Vidarbha, Marathwada and the rest of the state.
stateNotes.Gujarat: Article 371(2): development boards for Saurashtra and Kutch.
stateNotes.Nagaland: Article 371A: Parliament's laws on Naga religion, customary law, and land and resources apply only if the Assembly agrees.
stateNotes.Assam: Article 371B: a committee of the Assembly for the tribal areas.
stateNotes.Manipur: Article 371C: a committee of the Assembly for the hill areas.
stateNotes.Andhra Pradesh: Article 371D: equitable opportunities in jobs and education; 371E: a central university.
stateNotes.Sikkim: Article 371F: terms of Sikkim's merger in 1975, protecting existing laws.
stateNotes.Mizoram: Article 371G: protection of Mizo religion, customary law, and land, as in Nagaland.
stateNotes.Arunachal Pradesh: Article 371H: the Governor's special responsibility for law and order.
stateNotes.Goa: Article 371I: an Assembly of at least 30 members.
stateNotes.Karnataka: Article 371J: special provisions for the Hyderabad–Karnataka (Kalyana Karnataka) region.

layers.name: States formed after 1956
layers.note: Reorganisation did not end with 1956. Tap a state for its year.

stateNotes.Maharashtra: 1960: Bombay State split on linguistic lines.
stateNotes.Gujarat: 1960: Bombay State split on linguistic lines.

layers.name: Union Territories
layers.note: Eight UTs. Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have legislatures.

groups.label: Without a legislature
items: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

layers.name: Sex ratio extremes (Census 2011)
layers.note: Kerala had the highest sex ratio among states (1,084 women per 1,000 men); Haryana the lowest (879).

modules.name: Borders & internal security
modules.seo: India border states & internal security map for UPSC
modules.desc: Borders and internal security map of India for UPSC Mains: states on each international border and the force that guards it, the LWE belt, the North-East, coastal states and security hotspots.
modules.lead: Internal security answers start from geography: which states face which neighbour, who guards each border, and where insurgency and terror have struck. Tap a layer, then a state or a pin.

layers.name: Pakistan border (BSF)
layers.note: Guarded by the BSF; the Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir is held by the Army. Sir Creek in Gujarat is disputed.

layers.name: China border (ITBP)
layers.note: The Line of Actual Control is guarded by the ITBP, with the Army; it is undemarcated in all three sectors.

layers.name: Nepal border (SSB)
layers.note: Open border guarded by the SSB.

layers.name: Bhutan border (SSB)
layers.note: Open border guarded by the SSB.

layers.name: Bangladesh border (BSF)
layers.note: India's longest land border, guarded by the BSF; riverine stretches are hard to fence.

layers.name: Myanmar border (Assam Rifles)
layers.note: Guarded by the Assam Rifles; the Free Movement Regime and drug trafficking are key issues.

layers.name: Left Wing Extremism
layers.note: The core belt has shrunk sharply; check the latest MHA list of affected districts before quoting numbers.

groups.label: Affected earlier or at lower intensity

layers.name: Coastal states & UTs
layers.note: Nine coastal states and four coastal UTs; coastal security was rebuilt after 26/11.
items: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

layers.name: Security hotspots
layers.note: Places that recur in security answers.

items.name: Siachen
items.note: Highest battlefield; held by India since 1984 (Actual Ground Position Line).

items.name: Galwan valley
items.note: Ladakh; India–China clash, June 2020.

items.name: Pangong Tso
items.note: Ladakh; lake on the LAC, site of the 2020 stand-off.

items.name: Kargil
items.note: 1999 war against Pakistani intrusion.

items.name: Pulwama

items.name: Pathankot

items.name: Siliguri Corridor

items.name: Doklam
items.note: India–China stand-off on Bhutanese territory, 2017.

items.name: Tawang

modules.name: Environment overlays
modules.seo: Ramsar sites, tiger reserves & biosphere reserves map
modules.desc: Environment map of India for UPSC Mains: selected Ramsar sites, tiger reserves, UNESCO biosphere reserves, mangroves and coral reefs, with PYQ sketch drills. Selected sites, approximate locations.
modules.lead: Conservation answers are stronger with two or three correctly placed examples. These layers show selected, well-known sites, not complete lists, which change every year; pins are approximate.

layers.name: Ramsar sites (selected)
layers.note: Wetlands of international importance. Chilika and Keoladeo were India's first, in 1981; the list grows every year.

items.name: Chilika Lake
items.note: Odisha; brackish lagoon; one of India's first two Ramsar sites (1981).

items.name: Keoladeo
items.note: Rajasthan; bird sanctuary; first Ramsar sites with Chilika (1981).

items.name: Wular Lake
items.note: Jammu & Kashmir; large freshwater lake on the Jhelum.

items.name: Loktak Lake
items.note: Manipur; floating phumdis and Keibul Lamjao park.

items.name: Sambhar Lake
items.note: Rajasthan; India's largest inland salt lake.

items.name: Vembanad-Kol
items.note: Kerala; backwaters and below-sea-level farming.

items.name: East Kolkata Wetlands
items.note: West Bengal; treats the city's sewage through fisheries.

items.name: Sundarban Wetland
items.note: West Bengal; largest Ramsar site in India.

items.name: Bhitarkanika
items.note: Odisha; mangroves and saltwater crocodiles.

items.name: Point Calimere
items.note: Tamil Nadu; coastal wetland for migratory birds.

items.name: Harike
items.note: Punjab; at the Beas–Sutlej confluence.

items.name: Deepor Beel
items.note: Assam; Brahmaputra floodplain lake near Guwahati.

layers.name: Tiger reserves (selected)
layers.note: Project Tiger began in 1973 with Jim Corbett among the first reserves.

items.name: Jim Corbett
items.note: Uttarakhand; India's first national park (1936).

items.name: Kanha
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; saved the hard-ground barasingha.

items.name: Ranthambore
items.note: Rajasthan; dry deciduous forest.

items.name: Sundarbans Tiger Reserve
items.note: West Bengal; the only mangrove tiger habitat.

items.name: Periyar
items.note: Kerala; Western Ghats.

items.name: Bandipur
items.note: Karnataka; part of the Nilgiri landscape.

items.name: Kaziranga
items.note: Assam; also home to most of the world's one-horned rhinos.

items.name: Tadoba-Andhari
items.note: Maharashtra.

items.name: Panna
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; tigers reintroduced after local extinction; affected by the Ken–Betwa link.

items.name: Simlipal
items.note: Odisha; also a biosphere reserve.

items.name: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam
items.note: Andhra Pradesh–Telangana; India's largest tiger reserve.

items.name: Manas
items.note: Assam; World Heritage Site on the Bhutan border.

items.name: Gulf of Mannar

items.name: Sunderban
items.note: West Bengal; mangroves.

items.name: Nanda Devi

items.name: Pachmarhi

items.name: Similipal

items.name: Achanakmar-Amarkantak
